observation_summary: The TypeUtils.getTypeArguments method fails to correctly identify type arguments when a class implements an interface with specific type parameters while also defining its own type variables. The test case expects 2 type arguments to be resolved, but the method returns 0.
hypothesis: The algorithm within TypeUtils.getTypeArguments incorrectly skips classes that define their own type variables, failing to traverse the inheritance hierarchy to resolve type arguments for implemented interfaces.
prediction: The implementation of TypeUtils.getTypeArguments likely contains a conditional check that prematurely terminates the search or ignores classes that have their own type parameters, preventing the correct mapping of type variables.
experiment_rationale: The failure occurs during the reflection-based resolution of type arguments. Since the method is responsible for traversing the class hierarchy to map type variables to their concrete types, the logic for handling class inheritance and interface implementation is the most likely location for the defect.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a failure in the computational logic of the TypeUtils.getTypeArguments method. It incorrectly ignores classes that define their own type variables, which is a procedural error in the algorithm used to traverse the type hierarchy. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object), but rather an incorrect implementation of the type resolution algorithm.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'This case fails because the current code ignores the Other class due to its specifying its own type variables, which is obviously incorrect.'
The failing test shows TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class) returns size 0 instead of 2.
The class structure involves an interface 'This<K, V>' and a class 'Other<T> implements This<String, T>'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The capability exists, but the implementation of the resolution algorithm is flawed. It is not a missing design capability.
While there is likely a conditional check causing the skip, the root cause is the logic of the algorithm itself, not a missing validation or guard.
